items.prompt: A student pushes a box with a force of 30 N over a distance of 4 m. Calculate the work done.

points.text: Uses work done = force x distance moved in the direction of the force

items.prompt: Explain, in terms of energy transfers, why a moving car slows down when the brakes are applied.

points.text: Identifies friction between brake pads and discs (and tyres and road)
States kinetic energy is transferred to thermal energy in the brakes

items.prompt: A force of 12 N acts 0.25 m from a pivot. Calculate the moment of the force about the pivot.

points.text: Uses moment = force x perpendicular distance from the pivot
Correct value 3 N m with unit

items.prompt: Explain why the resultant force on a skydiver becomes zero as they reach terminal velocity.

points.text: States air resistance grows with speed until it equals the weight
Concludes equal and opposite forces give zero resultant force, so no acceleration

levels.label: Secure
levels.descriptor: Quantities, units and energy-transfer chains are all stated precisely.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: The physics is broadly right but a unit, quantity or link is missing.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.descriptor: Key quantities or transfers are confused or absent.
